title: Recover authoritative payment status before any new mutation

state.summary: The payment acknowledgement was lost and the authoritative commit outcome is initially unknown.
known_facts: No fresh payment mutation is permitted while the prior commit state is unknown.
constraints: Do not create a new payment mutation while the prior commit state is unknown

tension.summary: A blind retry could create a second financial effect if the first mutation already committed.

cause.summary: Transport acknowledgement loss leaves the commit outcome ambiguous.
supporting_signals: The payment acknowledgement was not received
cause.basis: Provider-neutral failure model: a commit and its transport acknowledgement can diverge.

confidence_assessment.rationale: The case deliberately models a lost acknowledgement after a possible commit; the duplicate-effect risk mechanism is explicit in the scenario.
alternative_explanations: The payment may not have committed
The payment may have committed but the response was lost

transition.trigger: Authoritative lookup using the original operation identity
transition.expected_consequence: Recover terminal payment status without creating another payment mutation.

participants.name: requesting-system
participants.goal: Complete exactly one intended payment safely
participants.risk: Duplicate effect if a fresh mutation is issued prematurely

participants.name: payment-state-source
participants.goal: Report authoritative status for the original operation identity
participants.risk: Status can be stale or temporarily unavailable

cooperation.shared_upside: Correct recovery without duplicate financial effects

action.summary: Recover authoritative payment status using the original operation identity before any new payment mutation.

review.summary: Authoritative lookup found the existing payment effect; no new payment mutation was issued.
review.actual_consequence: The existing effect was accepted and duplicate-effect exposure was closed for this provider-neutral case.
